title: Rigveda 9.89: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.89: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.89 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 718v-719r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>pro sya vahni̍ḥ pa̱thyā̍bhir asyān di̱vo na vṛ̱ṣṭiḥ pava̍māno akṣāḥ | sa̱hasra̍dhāro asada̱n ny a1̱̍sme mā̱tur u̱pasthe̱ vana̱ ā ca̱ soma̍ḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>THIS Chariot-horse hath moved along the pathways, and Pavamâna flowed like rain from heaven. With us hath Soma with a thousand currents sunk in the wood, upon his Mother's bosom.

Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.88.4 ‹na hi tvam ahi-nāmnām›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 719r (numbered 36r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.89.2 ‹-śyena-jūtaḥ duhe īm pitā›. Verse 9.89.1 ends on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 9.89.2-7 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 3, varga 25); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 719r
translation.original_text:
2rājā̱ sindhū̍nām avasiṣṭa̱ vāsa̍ ṛ̱tasya̱ nāva̱m āru̍ha̱d raji̍ṣṭhām | a̱psu dra̱pso vā̍vṛdhe śye̱najū̍to du̱ha ī̍m pi̱tā du̱ha ī̍m pi̱tur jām ||
3si̱ṁhaṁ na̍santa̱ madhvo̍ a̱yāsa̱ṁ hari̍m aru̱ṣaṁ di̱vo a̱sya pati̍m | śūro̍ yu̱tsu pra̍tha̱maḥ pṛ̍cchate̱ gā asya̱ cakṣa̍sā̱ pari̍ pāty u̱kṣā ||
4madhu̍pṛṣṭhaṁ gho̱ram a̱yāsa̱m aśva̱ṁ rathe̍ yuñjanty uruca̱kra ṛ̱ṣvam | svasā̍ra īṁ jā̱mayo̍ marjayanti̱ sanā̍bhayo vā̱jina̍m ūrjayanti ||
5cata̍sra īṁ ghṛta̱duha̍ḥ sacante samā̱ne a̱ntar dha̱ruṇe̱ niṣa̍ttāḥ | tā ī̍m arṣanti̱ nama̍sā punā̱nās tā ī̍ṁ vi̱śvata̱ḥ pari̍ ṣanti pū̱rvīḥ ||
6vi̱ṣṭa̱mbho di̱vo dha̱ruṇa̍ḥ pṛthi̱vyā viśvā̍ u̱ta kṣi̱tayo̱ haste̍ asya | asa̍t ta̱ utso̍ gṛṇa̱te ni̱yutvā̱n madhvo̍ a̱ṁśuḥ pa̍vata indri̱yāya̍ ||
7va̱nvann avā̍to a̱bhi de̱vavī̍ti̱m indrā̍ya soma vṛtra̱hā pa̍vasva | śa̱gdhi ma̱haḥ pu̍ruśca̱ndrasya̍ rā̱yaḥ su̱vīrya̍sya̱ pata̍yaḥ syāma ||
translation.text:
2King, he hath clothed him in the robe of rivers, mounted the straightest-going ship of Order. Sped by the Hawk the drop hath waxed in waters: the father drains it, drains the Father's offspring.
3They come to him, red, tawny, Lord of Heaven, the watchful Guardian of the meath, the Lion. First, Hero in the fight, he seeks the cattle, and with his eye the Steer is our protector.
4They harness to the broad-wheeled car the mighty Courser whose back bears meath, unwearied, awful. The twins, the sisters brighten him, and strengthen-these children of one damethe vigorous Racer.
5Four pouring out the holy oil attend him, sitting together in the same container. To him they flow, when purified, with homage, and still, from every side, are first about him.
6He is the buttress of the heavens, supporter of earth, and in his hand are all the people. Be the team's Lord a well to thee the singer: cleansed is the sweet plant's stalk for deed of glory.
7Fighting, uninjured come where Gods are feasted; Soma, as Vitra-slayer flow for Indra. Vouchsafe us ample riches very splendid may we be masters of heroic vigour.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 719r (numbered 36r by the scribe) (OPenn image 719, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.89.2 ‹-śyena-jūtaḥ duhe īm pitā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 719v (numbered 36v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.90.1 ‹-gacchan āyudhā sam-śiśānaḥ viśvā›. Verses 9.89.2-7 end on this page; 9.89.2 begins on fol. 718v (numbered 35v by the scribe).
